svg.text: CT6 Energy Monitor v0.1: EasyEDA connection guide (every part, every pin, every net)
Generated from the verified KiCad netlist (ERC 0 · DRC 0). In EasyEDA: place each part, then put a Net Label with the EXACT coloured name on each pin. Same name = connected.
Pins marked "no connect" stay empty. Power nets: use EasyEDA net labels (not power symbols) so the names match exactly: +5V, +3V3, +3V3A, GND, VB.
1 · Power input (5 V terminal or USB-C, power only)
+3V3 comes from the DevKit's own 3V3 pin; FB1 makes the clean analog rail +3V3A.
2 · Bias VB ≈ 1.50 V (MCP6002 unit A) + op-amp decoupling
U1 is one MCP6002 chip: unit A = bias buffer, unit B = voltage amplifier (section 3). R5 47Ω isolates the op-amp from C6.
3 · Mains voltage sensing ⚠ 230 V: keep ≥ 6.5 mm from all other copper, slot under T1
AC_* nets are LIVE. T1 (ZMPT101B) is the isolation barrier: primary pins 1-2 mains, secondary pins 3-4 low voltage.
4 · CT channel (CT1 shown; CT2–CT6 are identical, see table below)
JP jumper: shunt on pins 1-2 = mA CT (100A/50mA, burden IN, default); pins 2-3 = 1 V CT (30A/1V, burden OUT).
Two 1×22 female headers, rows 22.86 mm apart (MEASURE your DevKit). Pin 1 = antenna end. Unused pins: no connect.
M3 holes, no copper. H1 is inside the mains area: plastic screw.
7 · Full net list (check every net in EasyEDA's Design Manager against this)
Order check before sending to JLCPCB: DevKit row spacing & pinout · ZMPT101B pin grid 10.0 × 12.7 mm · screw-terminal wire entry · 6.5 mm mains creepage + slot · run EasyEDA DRC.
